extracted_experimental_details: LDL internalization measured by fluorescence intensity after 30-min incubation at 37°C. Compared wild-type, heterozygous p.(Pro955Ser), homozygous p.(Pro955Ser), and pathogenic p.(Arg3527Gln) controls. Biological replicates n=3 per group.
p2_source_location: Figure 3 legend: 'p<0.01 between control and each variant'
findings: The APOB p.(Pro955Ser) variant was found in 9.8% of FH probands (n=63/234) with an OR=4.9 (p=6.9×10⁻¹³).
Functional analysis showed reduced LDL internalization efficiency in hepatocytes for p.(Pro955Ser) compared to controls (p<0.01).
Dose-dependent effect observed: homozygous p.(Pro955Ser) showed greater impairment than heterozygous (p<0.01).

dimensions.name: disease_mechanism
dimensions.reason: Disease mechanism is clearly articulated: APOB p.(Pro955Ser) impairs LDL receptor-mediated internalization in hepatocytes, a well-established pathogenic mechanism in familial hypercholesterolemia. The variant's functional consequence (reduced LDL uptake) directly explains the disease phenotype.

dimensions.name: method_suitability
dimensions.reason: LDL internalization assay via fluorescence intensity measurement is highly appropriate for evaluating APOB function. This directly measures the molecular consequence of the variant in disease-relevant hepatocytes, aligning perfectly with the known pathogenic mechanism of impaired lipoprotein uptake in FH.

dimensions.name: experimental_validity
dimensions.reason: All experimental validity criteria met with high quality. Controls are comprehensive (normal + pathogenic), replicates adequate, method is validated and reliable, and positive controls are appropriately included. This represents robust experimental design.

dimensions.name: odds_path_validity
dimensions.reason: OddsPath = 3.387 (calculated from P1=0.098, P2=0.269). Both P1 and P2 are valid probabilities in (0,1). OddsPath value of 3.387 falls within the 3.0–20 range, mapping to PS3_supporting evidence strength. The reported strength classification as 'supporting' is CORRECT. However, the OddsPath is at the lower boundary of PS3_supporting; stronger functional evidence or higher OR would elevate to PS3_moderate (20–60 range).
suggestions: Consider whether additional functional assays (e.g., LDLR binding kinetics, protein stability studies) could strengthen the functional evidence toward PS3_moderate
Document the statistical power of the LDL internalization assay to justify confidence in the p<0.01 threshold

key_issues: OddsPath at lower boundary of PS3_supporting (3.387 vs. 3.0 threshold): marginal classification strength
P2 value (0.269) derived from qualitative p<0.01 statement rather than exact effect size; consider reporting actual percentage reduction in LDL uptake for precision
Single functional assay type (LDL internalization); complementary assays (e.g., LDLR binding, protein trafficking) would strengthen evidence
Dose-dependent effect (homozygous > heterozygous) is supportive but not quantified with exact fold-change values
No mention of allele frequency in general population (gnomAD/ExAC); need to verify this is not a common variant that would trigger BA1/BS1
recommendations: VALIDATE: Confirm APOB p.(Pro955Ser) allele frequency in gnomAD is <1% to exclude BA1/BS1 benign classification
ENHANCE: Report exact percentage reduction in LDL internalization (e.g., '45% reduction vs. wild-type') rather than relying on p-values alone for P2 calculation
STRENGTHEN: Add complementary functional assays such as LDLR binding affinity (surface plasmon resonance) or protein stability (thermal shift assay) to elevate evidence toward PS3_moderate
QUANTIFY: Provide fold-change values for homozygous vs. heterozygous comparison to better characterize dose-dependent effect
DOCUMENT: Include assay validation metrics (sensitivity, specificity, reproducibility coefficient of variation) to support method reliability claim
CLARIFY: Specify whether the 9.8% prevalence in FH probands represents a case-control comparison; if so, ensure control population is clearly defined and matched
